(Absent)
 *******
 JUDGMENT Petitioner asserting to be an injured suffered in a RTA filed petition under Section 166 of M.V.Act claiming compensation worth of Rs.25,00,000/- from the respondents, who are the owners and insurer of Bus bearing No.AR-02-6521, alleging that on 20.05.2022 at 9.30 p.m. when riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JS- 3201 on the road near Kaveri junction , Bengaluru , within the limits of Sadashivanagara police station, driver of Bus bearing No.AR-02-6521 drove the same negligently, dashed the same to the rear part of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JS-3201 , thereby caused accident , caused grievous injuries to the petitioner.
2. Petitioner took treatment at Prolife Multi Speciality hospital , Byatarayanapura, Bengaluru.

3. As on the date of accident petitioner being aged 25 years, used to earn Rs.38,000/p.m. by working as I.T. System Operator/Engineer at Cadabam hospital, Bengaluru .
4.

Regarding accident Sadashivanagara Traffic police registered crime No.45/2022 .
5.

In response to the notice, respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through his Advocate filed written statement denying the allegation regarding reason, mode of accident, nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner .
6. Inspite of service of notice , respondent No.1 driver of bus , respondent No.3 R.C.Owner of Bus bearing No.AR- 02-6521 remained absent.

7. On the basis of the pleadings on 07.07.2023 , this Authority has framed the following issues :
1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 20.05.2022 at about 09.30 p.m. near Kaveri Theatre junction, T.Chowdaiah road, Bengaluru , he met with an accident and sustained injuries, was due to actionable negligence act on the part of the driver of the Ashok Leyland bus bearing registration No.AR- 02-6521 as alleged?

Chethan vs Ravikumar P.K on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114515824/
2
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order ?
8. On 01.09.2023, 06.10.2023, 13.12.2023, 01.04.2024, petitioner deposed as PW1 and produced 21 documents at Exs.P.1 to P.21.

On 07.12.2024, 24.12.2024, 29.03.2025, petitioner produced the evidence of Dr.Shailesh A.V. Rao as PW2 and produced 2 documents at Ex.P.22 and P.23.
9.
I heard the arguments submitted on behalf of both the contesting parties and perused the records.

10. On the basis of material available in the file, my findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ....
In the affirmative Issue No.2...

Petitioner is entitle to Rs.6,26,311/-
with current and future interest at 6%p.a. as compensation from the respondents .
Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 11. Issue No.1 :- In the evidence petitioner/PW1 stated that on 20.05.2022 at 9.30p.m. when riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JS-3201(KA-02-JC-3201) on the road near Kaveri junction from P.G.Halli towards Ganganagar, driver of Bus bearing No.AR-02-6521 drove the same negligently,
dashed the same to the rear part of the motorcycle, thereby caused accident , caused grievous injuries to the petitioner.
12.
In the written statement respondent No.2 insurance company denied the allegation regarding reason , mode of accident.
13. In the cross-examination petitioner stated that on the date of accident he was moving from Cadabam hospital towards Ganganagar by riding motorcycle .
Petitioner stated that in Prolife Multi Speciality hospital, police have recorded his statement on which document made signature.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that there is no impediment to him and his friends to lodge complaint on the date of accident.
Petitioner stated that before the doctors of Prolife Multi Speciality hospital never stated the mode of accident.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that at the time of accident many vehicles were moving on the road.
Petitioner admitted that there is a junction on the road and in Ex.P.2 sketch the place of accident is noted at middle of the road.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that the accident took place solely due to his negligence as he dashed the motorcycle to the bus.
14. In the evidence PW2 Dr.Shailesh A.V. Rao stated nothing regarding reason and mode of the accident.
15. The copy of FIR shows that on 21.05.2022 on the basis of statement of petitioner Chethan, S/o.

Raju Poojari recorded in the hospital , Sadashivanagara police registered crime No.45/2022 against Chethan vs Ravikumar P.K on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114515824/
3 the driver of Bus bearing No.AR-02-6521 for having committed offence punishable uner Section 279, 337 of IPC.
16. Ex.P.1 is the copy of spot mahazar.
Ex.P.2 is the copy of sketch of place of accident.

Ex.P.3 is the copy of chargesheet filed by Sadashivanagar police in crime No.45/2022 against respondent No.1 Ravikumar P.K., S/o. Kumar P.N., driver of the Bus bearing No.AR-02-6521 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,338 of IPC .
P.4 is the copy of the wound certificate in which reason for the injuries are noted as RTA on 20.05.2022 at 9.30 near Kaveri Theater.
Ex.P.5 is the copy of Motor Vehicle Accident Report.
Ex.P.14 is the copy of the statement of the petitioner recorded on 21.05.2022 at Prolife Multi Speciality hospital .
Ex.P.15 is the copy of FIR.

Ex.P.16 is the copy of order sheet pertaining to C.C.No.2241/2022 registered on the file of MMTC-V, Bengaluru on the basis of Final Report submitted by Sadashivanagar Traffic police in crime No.45/2022 against respondent No.1,
Ravikumar, driver of Bus bearing No.AR- 02-6521 for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,338 of IPC which shows that in that case on 19.07.2022, respondent No.1 appeared before the Court pleaded guilty for having committed offence punishable under Section 279,338 of IPC and suffered sentence on payment of fine.
18. In this case respondents have not produced any type of evidence to disbelieve or rebut the evidence placed by the petitioner regarding reason and mode of accident.

Hence, I have concluded that on 20.05.2022 at 9.30p.m. when petitioner was riding motorcycle bearing No.KA-02- JS-3201(
KA-02-JC-3201) on the road near Kaveri junction , Bengaluru , within the limits of Sadashivanagara police station, respondent No.1/ Ravikumar negligently drove Bus bearing No.AR-02-6521, dashed the same to the rear part of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-JS-3201, thereby caused accident ,
caused grievous injuries to the petitioner.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.2:

In the evidence petitioner stated that in the accident he has suffered dislocation of left hip PIPKIN's type I, comminuted fracture neck of glenoid , C2/ C3 subluxation with unilateral face joint , took treatment at Prolife Multi Speciality hospital , Byatarayanapura as an inpatient from 21.05.2022 to 31.05.2022 by spending Rs.7,00,000/-.
Petitioner stated that as on the date of incident he used to earn Rs.38,000/p.m. by working as I.T. System Engineer/Operator at Cadabam hospital .
20. In the written statement respondent No.2 denied the nature and consequence of the injuries suffered by the petitioner.
21. In the cross-examination petitioner stated about treatment taken at Prolife Multi Speciality hospital as an inpatient for a period of 11 days.
Petitioner denied the suggestion that he never underwent surgery at Prolife Multi Speciality hospital .
Petitioner denied the suggestion that medical expenses were reimbursed through Health Insurance.
Petitioner denied the suggestion about non- spending of Rs.7,00,000/- and fabrication of documents marked at Ex.P.9.
Petitioner stated that after discharge from Prolife Multi Speciality hospital never taken further treatment in any hospital.

Petitioner admitted that receipts produced at Sl.No.3,4,7,8,56,57,58 & 59 at Ex.P.7 are Chethan vs Ravikumar P.K on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114515824/
4 advance receipts.
Petitioner denied the suggestion about reimbursement of medical expenses through employer at Cadabam hospital .
In the evidence PW1 stated about receipt of salary worth of Rs. 36,000/- for the month of February 2024.
22. In the evidence affidavit PW2 Dr.Shailesh A.V.Rao stated that on 29.10.2024 and 21.05.2022 when clinically examined the petitioner noticed that petitioner suffered disability at 10%.

23. In the evidence PW2 produced OPD record and cervical spine x-ray report at Ex.P.22 and P.23.
24.
In the cross-examination PW2 submitted that he neither treated the petitioner nor verified inpatient record .
PW2 stated that as on 21.11.2024 fractures of the petitioner are united.

25. Wound certificate, discharge summary , medical reports and other medical documents shows that in the accident petitioner suffered polytrauma, C2 jumped locked facet with C2-C3 subluxation,
fracture of left hip-displaced fracture of posterior column of left acetabulum, fracture of lateral border of left scapula, fracture of lateral end of left clavicle, took treatment at Prolife Multi Speciality hospital, Bengaluru as an inpatient from 21.05.2022 to 31.05.2022.
26.
In the copy of D.L. and Aadhar card marked at Ex.P.19 and 20, date of birth of petitioner is noted as 11.03.1998.

The medical bills shows that petitioner has spent approximately Rs.3,86,311/-
towards treatment.
In the file there are no documents to show reimbursement of medical bills or paying of medical expenses by either employer of the petitioner or any insurance company .

27. Under Certificate marked at Ex.P.9 Medical officer of Prolife Multi Speciality hospital certified that petitioner taken treatment for the injuries suffered in RTA for 10 days from 21.05.2022 to 31.05.2022 and he has been advised bed rest from 01.06.2022 to 0108.2022.
28.
As referred above, in the evidence petitioner submitted that during February 2024 received salary worth of Rs.36,000/-.
In this case petitioner has not produced documentary evidence regarding loss of salary or lorr of leave during treatment period.
29. As referred above, in the evidence and petition, petitioner asserted that he is working as IT System Operator/Engineer at Cadabams hospital .

30. Ex.P.18 are the salary slips of the petitioner issued by Anunitha (Cadabams) for the period from February 2022 to April 2022 shows that during that period petitioner being an employee of Anunitha Company (Cadabams) earned Rs.8,000/p.m. as basic , Rs.3,200/- as HRA, Rs.1,000/- as Local conveyance, Rs.23,396/- as basket allowance, totally Rs.35,596/- .
31. As referred above, in the evidence petitioner stated that during February 2024 he received salary worth of Rs.36,000/-.
32. In the evidence PW2 submitted that as on 21.11.2024 fracture of the petitioner are united.

In the file there are no evidence to show either loss of income or decrease in the income of the petitioner Chethan vs Ravikumar P.K on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114515824/
5 subsequent to the treatment taken for the injuries suffered in the accident.

Hence, I have inferred that the oral evidence of PW2, Dr.Shailesh A.V.Rao is insufficient to award compensation under the head of loss of future income (functional disability).
33.

Considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place , nature of the treatment taken by the petitioner , lack of documentary evidence regarding loss of leave of the petitioner during treatment period, status of the petitioner as an employee of Cadabams hospital , I award Rs.1,20,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.3,86,311/- (subject to arithmetical verification/confirmation) towards treatment charges, Rs.20,000/- towards attendant, conveyance and nourishment charges, Rs.1,00,000/- towards loss of amenities and future unhappiness.
34. Hence, I came to the conclusion that the petitioner is entitle to receive Rs.6,26,311/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., towards compensation from the respondents.

Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No.
1.
Pain and Sufferings Rs. 1,20,000-00 2.
Treatment charges Rs. 3,86,311-00 3. Attendant, conveyance and Rs. 20,000-00  nourishment charges 4. Loss of amenities and future Rs. 1,00,000-00  unhappiness.

On the basis of evidence placed by the petitioner , considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, length, place , nature of the treatment taken by the petitioner , I came to the conclusion that compensation assessed and awarded at Rs.6,26,311/- with current and future interest at 6% p.a., is just, proper and reasonable.
36. In the written statement , respondent No.2 insurance company admitted the subsistence of the policy with respect to Bus bearing No.AR-02-6521 as on the date of accident.
In the reply marked at Ex.P.6 submitted by Ramesh V.N. to the Investigation Officer to the notice under Section 133 of IMV Act Ramesh V.N. noted D.L. number of the respondent No.1 Ravikumar.
Hence, it is clear that as on the date of incident respondent No.3 does not violate any terms of the policy.

Hence, I came to the conclusion that the respondents being the driver, insurer and owner of Bus bearing No.AR-02-6521 are liable to pay the compensation and an award is to be passed directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence, I answer issue No.2 accordingly and pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of IMV Act is hereby partly allowed.
Chethan vs Ravikumar P.K on 11 April, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114515824/
6

The respondents shall either jointly or severally pay Rs.6,26,311/- (Rupees six lakhs twenty six thousand three hundred and eleven only) with current and future interest at the rate of 6% p.a., to petitioner towards compensation.
The respondent No.2, being the Insurer of the Bus bearing No.AR-02-6521 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest within 3 months from today.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire compensation amount and interest may be released to the petitioner by crediting the same to his bank account directly.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

(Dictated to the Stenographer, transcribed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 11th day of April , 2025)
(J.N.SUBRAMANYA) Chief Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Prl. M.A.C.T.
